question: What is the primary purpose of a patient referral form?

options.A: To document daily medication administration charts in the ward
options.B: To serve as a permanent financial receipt for hospital services
options.C: To ensure continuity of care between different health facilities
options.D: To replace the patient's individual bedside nursing care plan

explanation: The referral form acts as a formal bridge to maintain consistent patient care when moving between different healthcare levels. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T12#GNS225_U2_T12_h1)

question: A patient is sent to a tertiary hospital without a referral form. What is the most likely consequence?

options.A: Fragmented care and potential delays in proper diagnosis
options.B: Complete elimination of the patient's past medical history
options.C: Automatic waiver of all hospital registration fees
options.D: Immediate admission to the specialized intensive care unit

explanation: Lacking formal documentation prevents receiving clinicians from knowing prior treatments, leading to disjointed care. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T12#GNS225_U2_T12_h1)

question: Which detail is least necessary on a standard patient referral form?

options.A: The provisional diagnosis made at the primary center
options.C: The name and signature of the referring nurse
options.D: Vital signs measured prior to patient transport

explanation: Recreational habits do not directly impact acute clinical transfer decisions or emergency interventions. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T12#GNS225_U2_T12_h2)

question: Why must emergency treatments given before transit be written on the referral form?

options.A: To prove the primary nurse completed their shift duties
options.B: To bypass the need for a physical examination on arrival
options.C: To prevent accidental drug overdose at the receiving facility
options.D: To fulfill strict hospital billing and revenue collection rules

explanation: Knowing administered doses stops receiving doctors from blindly repeating medications like analgesics or intravenous fluids. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T12#GNS225_U2_T12_h2)

question: What is the critical action a nurse must take immediately before patient transit?

options.A: Collect full payment for the ambulance fuel
options.B: Schedule a follow-up appointment for six months later
options.D: Discharge the patient from the national health database

explanation: Stabilization is mandatory before moving any unstable patient to prevent clinical deterioration during transit. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T12#GNS225_U2_T12_h3)

question: Why is advance telephone communication with the receiving facility important during a referral?

options.A: To confirm available bed space and specialist readiness
options.B: To transfer funds electronically for emergency drugs
options.C: To book an appointment with the hospital administrative director
options.D: To negotiate the cost of specialized surgical procedures

explanation: Alerting the receiving team ahead of time prevents arrival delays and ensures emergency staff are prepared. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T12#GNS225_U2_T12_h3)

question: A community health nurse preparing a patient for transfer should primarily focus on which task?

options.A: Providing patient counseling and assembling an emergency travel kit
options.B: Issuing official government medical licenses to receiving doctors
options.C: Managing the financial accounts of the tertiary teaching hospital
options.D: Performing major emergency surgeries at the primary health center

explanation: Preparation involves counseling the family and ensuring travel safety equipment is packed and ready. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T12#GNS225_U2_T12_h4)

question: How does emotional counseling by the nurse affect the referral process?

options.A: It shortens the physical distance to the tertiary hospital
options.B: It completely eliminates the need for an ambulance escort
options.C: It reduces panic and improves patient cooperation during transit
options.D: It guarantees free medical treatment at the destination

explanation: Addressing fears helps calm patients and their relatives, making the stressful transfer process smoother. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T12#GNS225_U2_T12_h4)

question: What does a referral feedback loop involve?

options.A: Patients returning to primary clinics to pay outstanding utility bills
options.B: Receiving facilities returning clinical outcome notes to the originating clinic
options.C: Nurses checking patient attendance registers at local markets
options.D: Hospitals calling community leaders to request financial donations

explanation: Feedback ensures the primary nurse knows the diagnosis, treatment given, and ongoing care plan for the patient. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T12#GNS225_U2_T12_h5)

question: What is a major consequence of broken feedback loops in community health?

options.A: Primary nurses lose track of patient outcomes and follow-up needs
options.B: Tertiary hospitals receive increased funding from the government
options.C: Ambulance drivers refuse to transport emergency cases
options.D: Patients automatically recover without needing further medications

explanation: Without feedback, community nurses cannot provide proper home-based rehabilitation or post-discharge monitoring. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T12#GNS225_U2_T12_h5)

question: Which factor is a major logistical barrier to emergency referrals in rural Nigeria?

options.A: Excessive availability of modern helicopters in every village
options.B: Poor road infrastructure and lack of functional ambulances
options.C: An oversupply of free medications blocking clinic storage rooms
options.D: Too many trained medical specialists at primary health centers

explanation: Bad roads and scarce transport vehicles delay critical patient transfers from rural communities. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T12#GNS225_U2_T12_h6)

question: How do out-of-pocket payment systems affect patient compliance with referrals?

options.A: Tertiary hospitals waive all fees for community referrals
options.B: Transportation becomes free of charge for emergency cases
options.C: Patients immediately arrive at tertiary centers with excess cash
options.D: Patients often refuse referrals due to fear of high hospital bills

explanation: Financial hardship forces many indigent patients to stay at home or seek unverified alternative care instead. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T12#GNS225_U2_T12_h6)

question: Why should primary health clinics keep duplicate copies of outgoing referral forms?

options.A: To sell old patient records to local commercial printing shops
options.B: For clinical audits, legal protection, and record tracking
options.C: To use as scrap paper for administrative office notes
options.D: To replace the national census population data collection

explanation: Duplicate copies provide proof of care and allow facilities to evaluate referral trends and outcomes. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T12#GNS225_U2_T12_h7)

question: What makes a referral logbook useful for a clinic supervisor?

options.A: It stops patients from complaining about long waiting hours
options.B: It helps identify recurring emergency trends and operational gaps
options.C: It guarantees an increase in the monthly staff salary budget
options.D: It automatically repairs broken clinic windows and doors

explanation: Reviewing logs shows managers which conditions are most common and where transit delays frequently occur. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T12#GNS225_U2_T12_h7)
